author: Marcus Fitzsimmons
title: Blount County's early voting trend forecasts strong turnout for midterms - NewsBreak
text:
By Marcus Fitzsimmons ,
41 minutes ago
A strong turnout in the first week of Early Voting has Blount County on a record pace for a midterm election cycle.
The Blount County Election Commission reviewed the first week’s totals then set times and dates for procedures following the Nov. 3 Election Day during their October meeting on Wednesday at the courthouse.
The trends observed for the first week’s totals continued Wednesday with daily totals running 400 to 600 ballots cast ahead of the 2022 election. As of the close of polls on Wednesday evening, 12,467 ballots have been completed compared to 9,103 in 2022 at the seven day mark. The early trend forecasts that 2026 could be much more like the 2018 midterm when more than 46,000 votes were cast rather than 2022 when just over 39,000 voters took part.With just over 100,000 voters currently registered in the county, Blount might approach a 50% turnout if the trend holds.
The ballot for the Nov. 3 election contains the general races for state and federal offices, special elections for county Board of Education in District 7 and County Commission Seat 4-C, the mayor’s race and alderman races for Louisville, the general elections for Alcoa city commissioners and Board of Education as well as Maryville City Council and Board of Education. It also contains votes on three proposed amendments to the state Constitution.
Five early voting locations are open — Pellissippi State, Blount County Public Library, Blount County Operations Center, Everett Recreation Center and Providence Baptist Church. Any Blount County resident can use any of the locations. Early voting ends on Thursday, Oct. 29. Election Day is Tuesday, Nov. 3, and voters must use their assigned precincts on that day. The library is again the most popular early voting location, topping 800 voters per day this week. The Blount County Operations Center on McArther Road has been the slowest so far and had little to no wait time for voters wishing to use the Early Voting locations.
WHAT TO BRING: Tennesseans voting early or on Election Day must bring valid photo identification with them to the polls. A driver’s license or photo ID issued by the Tennessee Department of Safety and Homeland Security, by Tennessee state government or by the federal government are acceptable even if they are expired. College IDs are not acceptable. Learn more about what types of ID are acceptable via https://sos.tn.gov/elections/voter-id-requirements or call the Division of Elections at 1-877-850-4959.
BEFORE YOU GO: There are multiple variations on the ballot in Blount County to meet all the various state, county and municipal boundaries. Voters who want to check races on their ballot can visit www.blounttn.gov/447/Election-Commission to see a sample ballot. The state also offers a smartphone app, GoVoteTN, that allows users to look up a sample ballot, polling location, elected officials, and other useful voter information by their address. The three constitutional amendments are long and reading them in advance will save time and screen aggravation.
BONA FIDE: With no party primaries involved, there is no bona fide form to sign for this election.
SCHEDULE: The commission anticipates that the Provisional Counting Board will be needed and meet on Nov. 9. The need is determined by the number of provisional ballots in the ballot boxes on Election Night. Generally when provisional exceed 100, the board is used to supplement the process. The audit will be Nov. 10 and certification of the county’s results will take place on Nov. 18 when the commission holds its monthly meeting.
